title: Recall service-model decisions
summary: Reconstruct each choice from its operational requirements, without an answer tray. These are original teaching scenarios, not exam questions.

kernel-control.clue: A required guest-kernel change and customer-managed patching rule out a provider-controlled runtime. Which service-model abbreviation preserves that operating-system authority?

managed-web-runtime.clue: A team must deploy its own web code but does not want guest-OS operations. The service supplies and maintains the supported runtime. Which service-model abbreviation fits?

finished-mail.clue: The company wants ready-to-use mail, with vendor application updates and customer user onboarding, rather than an application-development environment. Which service-model abbreviation fits?

os-maintenance.clue: The team explicitly retains guest-OS installation and maintenance as part of its migration plan. Which service-model abbreviation matches that responsibility?

managed-database.clue: A team designs its own database schema but delegates database-platform and guest-OS operations to a managed service. Which service-model abbreviation fits?

finished-expenses.clue: Staff need a finished expense product, with the vendor maintaining the application and customers managing their data and access. Which service-model abbreviation fits?

legacy-os.clue: A legacy migration cannot surrender guest-OS administration because required system changes remain the customer’s job. Which service-model abbreviation fits?

app-development.clue: The requirement is to build and deploy custom application logic on a managed development platform, with OS and runtime upkeep delegated to the host. Which service-model abbreviation fits?
